issues.title: General spectral-convergence overclaim

failure_location.quote: Our key contributions are proofs of the convergence of the approximating operator and its spectrum under non-restrictive conditions.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract advertises convergence of the approximating operator and its spectrum. The introduction specifies subsequential eigenpair convergence, while the dictionary and joint-limit theorems identify a limiting pair with an exact eigenpair only when the weak eigenfunction limit is nonzero. General spectrum-convergence wording overstates that conditional spectral contribution. The subjective adjective non-restrictive is not the basis of this issue.
issues.overall_effect: The spectral summary is broader than the conditional subsequential eigenpair results it describes. It can suggest setwise spectral convergence, approximation of every exact spectral point, or general absence of spectral pollution, which these results do not establish. A comparable conditional spectral-approximation contribution survives the prose repair; other theorem and proof issues remain separate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the general spectrum-convergence claim by the supported conditional statement: spectral results concern subsequences of approximate eigenpairs, with identification as exact eigenpairs conditional on nonzero weak limits and the stated hypotheses. Explain that this does not establish general setwise spectral convergence, approximation of every exact spectral point, or general absence of spectral pollution. Align the introductory summary with that qualification without changing the formal statements for this prose root.
issues.why_classification: The correction narrows a substantive advertised guarantee, so a short prose edit alone does not justify minor. Nevertheless, a recognizably comparable conditional spectral-approximation contribution survives, and this root requires neither new proof architecture nor alteration of the formal statements. The complete repair therefore has limited rather than major mathematical loss and supports moderate. This does not certify the separate spectral theorems.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: We also prove that in some cases eigenpairs of the approximating operators weakly converge to eigenpairs of the exact operator{, in others they do not}.

issues.title: Missing null-set preservation for Koopman operators

failure_location.quote: where the operator $\Kk \colon L^\infty(\mathbb{X}) \to L^\infty(\mathbb{X})$ is known as the \emph{Koopman operator}.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As before, we consider the state space $(\mathbb{X}, \Bb, \mu)$ and write $\Ff := L^2(\mathbb{X}, \mu)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that an arbitrary deterministic flow Φ induces K:L-infinity(X)→L-infinity(X). On an L-infinity space, however, functions are equivalence classes modulo μ-null sets, and the old source imposes no condition ensuring that Φ pulls null sets back to null sets. For Lebesgue measure on [0,1], the constant map Φ(x)=0 and the two representatives 0 and 1_{0} define the same L-infinity element but their compositions are respectively 0 and 1. Thus the claimed operator is not well-defined; the missing material qualification is null-set preservation or a pointwise function-space formulation.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's stated Koopman and Perron–Frobenius coverage includes flows for which the underlying operator on the chosen almost-everywhere space is undefined. The abstract operator results remain conditional on being supplied a genuine operator.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Distinguish pointwise observables from almost-everywhere equivalence classes. Define composition by Φ on pointwise bounded measurable functions, and state that it descends to an operator on L∞(μ) only when Φ is μ-nonsingular, meaning μ(Φ⁻¹(N))=0 for every μ-null set N. Apply the same qualification whenever the later abstract framework treats the Koopman operator as an operator on an almost-everywhere function space.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine well-definedness defect rather than a transcription error, but it is resolved by a standard local qualification or pointwise-space formulation. It does not alter the approximation method, conclusions, rates, or proofs once a genuine operator is supplied.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Given a measure $\mu$ on $\X$, if $\Phi$ preserves $\mu$-null sets, one can extend the Koopman operator to $\Kk \colon L^\infty(\X) \to L^\infty(\X)$.

issues.title: Ill-defined empirical projection operator
issues.failure_explanation: The sampling map records only function values, so equality of two empirical representatives does not imply equality of their sampled operator values. For example, take the uniform measure on [0,1], A=d/dx, dictionary {1,x}, and M=1. For every sampled x_1, the dictionary combination v=x-x_1 has zero empirical value but Av=1 has nonzero empirical value. Thus the rule defining the induced empirical operator sends an empirical zero representative to a nonzero value, and the proof's use of linearity on empirical equivalence classes is invalid.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed empirical projection is not an operator on the stated empirical space when sampling is non-injective, and the empirical-operator identity in the exact-approximation corollary is consequently undefined. The matrix estimator and its later large-sample interpretation on the original dictionary space are not defeated by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the sampled-value quotient used as the empirical domain by the empirical graph space spanned by the pairs (sampled ψᵢ, sampled Aψᵢ). Define the induced map on this graph space by sending each such pair to sampled Aψᵢ, formulate the projection as a map from the graph space into the sampled dictionary space, and redo the well-definedness proof and the exact-approximation corollary in that setting. The matrix estimator may then continue to be analyzed on the original dictionary space for the large-sample results.
issues.why_classification: A proof-line edit cannot make A descend through the noninjective sampling map, and merely assuming an invertible empirical Gram matrix would discard the natural and expressly advertised singular-sampling regime. The empirical graph-space construction preserves a recognizably comparable projection statement and its corollary, but it is a contained, nontrivial replacement of the domain and proof, so it exceeds a minor repair without requiring global reconstruction.

issues.title: Biased one-batch noisy estimator
issues.failure_explanation: With g=Ψ+η and centered noise, E[gg†]=G_N+E[ηη†], not G_N, unless the dictionary noise has zero covariance. Likewise, E[cg†] can contain a ξ-η cross-covariance. Consequently the empirical matrices generally concentrate around perturbed matrices rather than G_N and C_N, so the old premise used to prove concentration of the estimator around A_N is false and increasing M does not remove the bias.
issues.overall_effect: The noisy error estimate and the derived noisy order-of-convergence theorem can claim arbitrarily small error around A_N even though the one-batch estimator generally has a nonzero asymptotic bias.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the population identities to E[gg†]=G_N+Sigma_eta and E[cg†]=C_N+Sigma_xi_eta. Withdraw both the arbitrarily accurate A_N guarantee for the stated one-batch estimator at fixed dictionary-noise level and its dependent noisy order-of-convergence claim. Where suitable moment or tail conditions justify concentration, state convergence to the biased population operator and include the nonvanishing population bias in any A_N error estimate. Recovering consistency for A_N by covariance subtraction or independent replicate cross-products requires additional supplied noise information or repeat observations, a changed estimator, and an explicitly revised theorem and data contract.
issues.why_classification: The existing estimator is inconsistent in an ordinary included fixed-noise regime: for psi=1, A=Id, independent centered dictionary noise of variance one, and zero operator noise, its scalar estimate tends to 1/2 instead of A_N=1. A bias-floor bound therefore removes convergence to the stated target, not merely a constant or a modest rate improvement. The independent-replicate repair previously used to justify moderate changes the explicit only-have-access-to data contract; the second observation is not obtainable by reusing the first, and unknown noise covariance is not supplied either. Contained debiasing work for an augmented observation model does not preserve the original theorem's guarantee. The loss of consistency in the original model makes serious appropriate under the existing policy, without relying on the independent truncation-probability defect.

issues.title: Incorrect perturbation range
issues.failure_explanation: Writing a=||G_N^{-1}||, invertibility and the displayed factor-two inverse bound require aδ<1/2. The old statement instead permits δ<a/2, which does not imply this when a>1 and can even allow aδ≥1. Thus the proof only supports the range δ<(2a)^{-1}, not the stated range.
issues.overall_effect: For admissible Gram matrices with large inverse norm, the noisy proposition permits perturbations for which invertibility and the claimed inverse-error estimate are not established.
issues.why_classification: The missing inverse exponent is uniquely forced by the earlier Gram-matrix perturbation lemma and by the displayed Neumann-series denominator 1−‖G_N⁻¹‖δ. An adept reader can make this transcriptional correction directly, and no inference, construction, or guarantee in the valid range needs alteration.

issues.title: Missing M-fold conditioning probability

failure_location.quote: Now, by definition of $\tl{\mathbb{P}}$, we have that $\tl{p}_N\tl{\mathbb{P}}\leq \mathbb{P}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing E_m for the truncation event of sample m, the conditional measure is based on the event intersecting E_m over all m. Assumption noise assumption makes these events independent and each has probability tilde p_N, so the conditioning event has probability tilde p_N^M. The old conversion multiplies the conditional probability by only tilde p_N, and therefore tilde p_N>p does not ensure the claimed unconditional confidence p.
issues.overall_effect: The unconditional confidence level in the noisy error bound can be much smaller than claimed, and the same incorrect calibration propagates to the noisy order-of-convergence theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For the joint truncation event E=⋂ₘEₘ, use P(E)=p̃_N^M. Require p̃_N^M>p, set the needed conditional confidence to p/p̃_N^M, and replace p/p̃_N by p/p̃_N^M throughout the noisy proposition and the dependent order-of-convergence theorem. For unbounded noise, choose the truncation threshold as a function of M, or use an appropriate direct tail concentration bound, and recompute the resulting sample-size dependence.
issues.why_classification: The old per-sample condition p̃_N>p can still leave the asserted unconditional confidence exponentially small in M. A complete repair therefore changes the central confidence calibration and, for unbounded noise, requires reoptimizing the truncation threshold and propagating its effect through the sample bound. This is contained work with a comparable high-probability theorem surviving, but it is more than routine no-loss bookkeeping.

issues.title: Invalid varying-vector projection step
issues.failure_explanation: Assumption projection assumption states that (Id-P_N)g tends to zero for every fixed g. It does not imply that (Id-P_N)A f_N tends to zero in norm when f_N varies with N. For instance, on l2 with F_N=span{e_1,...,e_N}, the unilateral shift and graph-normalized f_N=e_N give A_N f_N=0 while the residual has nonvanishing norm. The proof only needs its pairing with fixed g, which vanishes after moving the self-adjoint projection onto g and using boundedness of A f_N.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not justify the vanishing residual term needed to identify a nonzero weak limit as an eigenfunction of A.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Do not claim norm convergence of (I−P_{F_{N_i}})Af_{N_i}. For each fixed g, use self-adjointness of the orthogonal projection to write ⟨(I−P_{F_{N_i}})Af_{N_i},g⟩=⟨Af_{N_i},(I−P_{F_{N_i}})g⟩, and bound this by ‖Af_{N_i}‖‖(I−P_{F_{N_i}})g‖. The first factor is uniformly bounded by the graph normalization and the second tends to zero by the projection assumption.
issues.why_classification: The proof contains a genuine invalid inference about a varying vector, so it is not a typo. Nevertheless, a short and standard projection-duality argument establishes exactly the scalar limit the proof needs under the existing assumptions, preserving the theorem and all its guarantees without loss.
